text:
Friendship is constant in all other things
Save in the office and affairs of love:
Therefore all hearts in love use their own tongues;
Let every eye negotiate for itself
And trust no agent; for beauty is a witch
Against whose charms faith melteth into blood.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: When it comes to what you want most, people speak for themselves. Do not send an agent for your own dreams.

text: Well, everyone can master a grief but he that has it.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Everyone has advice for your pain until it is theirs.

text: God hath blessed you with a good name: to be a well-favoured man is the gift of Fortune; but to write and read comes by Nature.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Looks are luck. Skill is what you actually build.

text: Shall quips and sentences and these paper bullets of the brain awe a man from the career of his humour?
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Other people's jokes and opinions are paper bullets. Do not let them turn you off your course.

text:
One doth not know
How much an ill word may empoison liking.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: One bad word at the wrong time can sour something good. Watch what you say.

text: Thou shouldst rather ask if it were possible any villainy should be so rich; for when rich villains have need of poor ones, poor ones may make what price they will.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Powerful people who need you will pay what you ask. Know your price.

text: All this I see, and I see that the fashion wears out more apparel than the man.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Chasing fashion costs more than the clothes themselves.

text: Time goes on crutches till love have all his rites.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: When you want something badly, every hour drags.

text: No, sure, my lord, my mother cried; but then there was a star danced, and under that was I born.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Rough start, lucky star. Where you began does not decide how you live.

text: Nay, if they lead to any ill, I will leave them at the next turning.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Follow the leaders only as far as they stay right, then turn off.

text: O! what men dare do! what men may do! what men daily do, not knowing what they do!
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: People do terrible things all day without knowing what they are doing. Pay attention.

text:
That what we have we prize not to the worth
Whiles we enjoy it, but being lack’d and lost,
Why, then we rack the value, then we find
The virtue that possession would not show us
Whiles it was ours.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: You only see what something was worth once it is gone. Value it while you have it.

text:
Time hath not yet so dried this blood of mine,
Nor age so eat up my invention,
Nor fortune made such havoc of my means,
Nor my bad life reft me so much of friends,
But they shall find, awak’d in such a kind,
Both strength of limb and policy of mind,
Ability in means and choice of friends,
To quit me of them throughly.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Age and bad luck have not drained me. When pushed, I still have strength and a plan.

text:
I pray thee peace! I will be flesh and blood;
For there was never yet philosopher
That could endure the toothache patiently,
However they have writ the style of gods
And made a push at chance and sufferance.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: No philosopher ever stayed calm through a toothache. Pain is not a thing you out-think.

text: What, courage, man! What though care killed a cat, thou hast mettle enough in thee to kill care.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Worry kills cats. You have more fight in you than your worry does.

text: In a false quarrel there is no true valour.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Fighting for the wrong reason takes no real courage.

text: If a man do not erect in this age his own tomb ere he dies, he shall live no longer in monument than the bell rings and the widow weeps.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 5 Scene 2
plain: If you do not make your own mark while alive, the world forgets you in an hour.

text: In brief, since I do purpose to marry, I will think nothing to any purpose that the world can say against it; and therefore never flout at me for what I have said against it, for man is a giddy thing, and this is my conclusion.
location: Much Ado About Nothing, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: People change their minds. I changed mine, and I am done apologizing for it.

text:
But I will wear my heart upon my sleeve
For daws to peck at: I am not what I am.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: The cynic's creed. Wear your heart on your sleeve and the crows will peck it, so Iago hides himself.

text:
’Tis the curse of service,
Preferment goes by letter and affection,
And not by old gradation, where each second
Stood heir to the first.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Promotions often go by who likes you, not who earned it. Know that going in.

text:
What cannot be preserved when fortune takes,
Patience her injury a mockery makes.
The robb’d that smiles steals something from the thief;
He robs himself that spends a bootless grief.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Smile at the thing that took from you and you take something back. Grieving for nothing only robs you twice.

text:
But words are words; I never yet did hear
That the bruis’d heart was pierced through the ear.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Words alone do not heal a broken heart.

text:
The tyrant custom, most grave senators,
Hath made the flinty and steel couch of war
My thrice-driven bed of down: I do agnize
A natural and prompt alacrity
I find in hardness, and do undertake
This present wars against the Ottomites.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Hardship becomes home when you live in it long enough. I find my energy in hard conditions.

text:
She lov’d me for the dangers I had pass’d,
And I lov’d her that she did pity them.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: She loved him for what he survived, and he loved her for caring. That is the whole spell.

text:
I saw Othello’s visage in his mind,
And to his honours and his valiant parts
Did I my soul and fortunes consecrate.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: She saw his character first, then gave everything to it.

text: ’Tis in ourselves that we are thus or thus. Our bodies are gardens, to the which our wills are gardeners.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: You are what you tend. You choose what grows in you.

text: There are many events in the womb of time which will be delivered.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: A lot is still coming that you cannot see yet.

text:
Keep up your bright swords, for the dew will rust them.
Good signior, you shall more command with years
Than with your weapons.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Put the blade away. Authority comes from years and character, not from threats.

text:
Not I; I must be found.
My parts, my title, and my perfect soul
Shall manifest me rightly.
location: Othello, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Do not hide. Who you are and what you have done will speak for you.

text: Reputation, reputation, reputation! O, I have lost my reputation! I have lost the immortal part of myself, and what remains is bestial.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Your name is the part of you that outlives the bad night. Guard it.

text: Reputation is an idle and most false imposition, oft got without merit and lost without deserving. You have lost no reputation at all, unless you repute yourself such a loser.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Reputation is a rumor. You only lose it if you agree you have lost it.

text: O God, that men should put an enemy in their mouths to steal away their brains! That we should with joy, pleasance, revel, and applause, transform ourselves into beasts!
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: We cheer ourselves on while drinking away our own judgment.

text:
How poor are they that have not patience!
What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
Thou know’st we work by wit, and not by witchcraft,
And wit depends on dilatory time.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Nothing heals overnight. Good work depends on time, so be patient.

text:
My blood begins my safer guides to rule,
And passion, having my best judgement collied,
Assays to lead the way.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: When anger takes the wheel, judgment goes dark. Notice the switch.

text:
Let’s teach ourselves that honourable stop,
Not to outsport discretion.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Know where to stop. Do not out-party your own discipline.

text:
I am not merry, but I do beguile
The thing I am, by seeming otherwise.
location: Othello, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Sometimes you act cheerful to get through. It is not lying, it is how you carry it.
